resolution: 3 inch (0.25 US survey ft per pixel)
crs: EPSG:2232, NAD83 / Colorado Central (ftUS); world files are .tfw

bands.finding: Band 4 is NOT near-infrared, measured 2026-08-17. NDVI computed as (B4-R)/(B4+R) is negative everywhere: parkland -0.037, pavement -0.080, roofprints -0.088 over 1.36M sampled pixels. Parkland is the only layer where B4 exceeds red, so the band carries a weak vegetation signal, but true NIR over canopy gives +0.3 to +0.8 -- a 0.04 separation is not NIR. Treat this product as RGB plus an unspecified fourth band. There is no free NDVI here, so vegetation discrimination from this imagery needs segmentation or a different product.
bands.note: PIL reports mode RGB and silently drops band 4; tifffile reads all four. Anything sampling this imagery through PIL is reading three bands without being told.

registration.attempted: cross-correlation of a LiDAR building mask against image gradients over a 300 m crop, +/- 6 ft search
registration.result: peak correlation 0.0724 at (-0.61, +0.61) m against 0.0707 at zero shift -- a 2% improvement, which is noise, not a measurement. No offset is claimed.
registration.suspected_cause: these are conventional orthophotos rather than true orthos, so building tops are displaced by relief and the very edges being correlated are smeared. In a downtown of tall buildings that effect is large.
registration.next: register on ground-level features only -- road markings, kerb lines, crossings -- where relief displacement is zero.
